title: What People Actually Build With Agents
description: Nine launches where the agent is not the product: websites, videos, study plans, internal tools and document pipelines built end to end.
tldr: The most telling recent launches are the ones where the agent disappears into the output. Nine of them build a website from a sentence, record a tutorial video of your real app, turn your notes into a study plan, host the internal tools your colleagues built, and convert documents into clean Markdown.
content:
# What People Actually Build With Agents

Most agent tooling is aimed at people who write code. These nine launches are aimed at the output instead: a website, a video, a study plan, an internal tool, a clean Markdown file. In each case the agent is plumbing, and what ships is the thing it made.

## A home for the apps your colleagues built

[[link:/tools/1975|Pando]] deploys and shares apps, turning the tools your team builds with AI into tools everyone can use, each placed behind access control from the start so you only share with the people who need it. The problem it names is familiar: people across a company are building their own tools with assistants, IT has nowhere safe to host them and no time to review each one, so they end up on laptops and personal cloud accounts.

## A free agent that writes and runs it

[[link:/tools/1998|Lemoncode]] is a free coding agent. You describe what you want and it writes the code, runs it and shows the result, with a preview, the list of changed files and the commands it ran. It also automates workflows by connecting to GitHub, Slack, Notion, Gmail, Jira, Linear and more than 1,500 other apps plus your own MCP servers, once or on a schedule. The interesting part is the app catalogue: an agent that can act outside the repository is a different product from one that cannot.

## A WordPress site from one sentence

[[link:/tools/2005|CanvoWP]] is a free WordPress plugin where you describe your website in plain English and the agent builds it: it designs the pages, writes real WordPress templates and content, and checks its own work at desktop and mobile widths. Every feature is unlocked with no paid tier and no licence key, output is plain HTML, CSS, JavaScript and PHP in your own uploads folder, and existing SEO, forms, shop and search plugins carry on working.

## Video editing where the footage already is

[[link:/tools/1980|Cutmark]] is a local-first video production workspace for people and agents. You record talking-head video and keep the source files on your Mac, then work with the agent you already use on scripts, storyboards, edits, review notes, thumbnails and post drafts. It supports [[link:/tools/1487|Claude Code]], Codex, pi and opencode in its in-app chat and exposes the same workspace over MCP. Local-first matters more in video than anywhere else, because the source files are enormous.

## A tutorial video recorded on your machine

[[link:/tools/2018|ScreenCI]] makes tutorial videos of your app from one prompt. You describe a feature and paste the prompt into your coding agent, and it records a narrated walkthrough of your real app for your help center, docs, social media or the product itself. It works with any agent that runs shell commands and is free to try with no account. Documentation that records itself is the obvious end state here.

## SaaS reduced to its primitives

[[link:/tools/2020|The Last SaaS]] is a headless SaaS for agents and assistants: an experiment in reducing every SaaS app to records, files, access and background work, so Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant can build on those primitives through MCP, CLI or API. Records are validated when saved, files can be shared with temporary links, and an agent can be given its own service account, permissions and API token.

## Is this picture real?

[[link:/tools/2007|Checkobot]] is an AI image detector. You show it a photo and it looks for AI generation, AI edits and face swaps, then tells you what it found and why, with two detectors taking a look. You get three free checks a day with no sign-up, and on free checks images are checked in memory and never stored. As generated output floods in, the checking tools become part of the pipeline rather than an afterthought.

## Documents into clean Markdown

[[link:/tools/2002|MarkItDown AI]] converts PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, CSV, JSON and XML into clean Markdown, preserving headings, lists and tables. The basic tier runs locally in your browser with no upload at all, while advanced handles scanned or complex layouts. Conversion is the unglamorous step most agent pipelines need before anything else can happen.

## Your notes into a study plan

[[link:/tools/2001|LongTerMemory]] turns your own materials into an AI study plan with daily sessions and smart reviews. You import PDFs, docs, slides, web links, notes and photos, and it produces auto-generated quizzes, chat over your notes, image OCR for photographed pages, spaced repetition and mnemonics. Access is a one-time purchase rather than a subscription, which is unusual enough to mention.

## The through line

In every one of these the agent is not what you buy. What you buy is a site that exists, a video that is recorded, a document that is readable, a plan you can follow. That is usually the sign the category has stopped being a demo.
